title: Command contracts

ground.note: The operator's brief: the library, the seven settled points (2026-10-30, amended 2026-11-02), what is out of scope.
The mod this spec is a prerequisite of: it reads `artifact status`, `plans overview` and the run list as JSON only, against published schemas.

Every command is a Commander command built in buildProgram; per-command `--json` options on ls and the plans family; the phase guard runs in a preAction hook and exits 1; cliDocs long help is attached after registration.
`--usage` is intercepted before Commander; any uncaught error prints `Unexpected error: …` and exits 1, the same code Commander uses for an unknown option.
`plans overview --json` prints `JSON.stringify(overview, null, 2)` with no `$schema`; a failed architecture provider is a warning on stderr in both modes.

`plans lint --json` prints the unversioned report and still exits 1 when a finding is an error: a document and a non-zero exit together; `plans status --json` prints `{ report, orphanRecords }` unversioned.
`phax ls --json` prints the versioned `run-list` document (`$schema` .../run-list/0.26.0.json); there is no `phax runs list` command, the brief's name for it.
`artifact decide --verdicts … --json` prints its report on one compact line, unversioned; `--json` without `--verdicts` is refused with exit 12.
Generated from the Commander tree; 65 commands; documents per-command exit codes (2 config, 12 artifact refusal, 1 phase guard, …) and names no code for an unknown option or an unexpected error.
Every published format is exported with JSONSchema.make and snapshotted per release under snapshots/<format>/<version>.schema.json.

context:
phax's commands are Commander commands, registered one by one in the CLI's program and each printing what it chooses. Nine of the 65 commands in `phax.usage.kdl` take `--json`. `phax ls --json` prints a versioned `run-list` document. `phax plans overview --json`, `phax plans lint --json` and `phax plans status --json` print unversioned documents. `phax artifact decide --verdicts … --json` prints its report on one compact line. `phax artifact status` prints only text. An unknown option or command is refused by Commander with exit 1. An uncaught error prints `Unexpected error: …` and also exits 1. The phase guard refuses with exit 1 too. `phax.usage.kdl` is generated by walking the live Commander tree, with long help and examples from the CLI docs table and completion from the completers table. The brief calls the run list `phax runs list`, but the command is `phax ls`, and this spec names it so. Renaming it would change what the command declares in `phax --usage`, which the operator settled stays the same.

The operator wrote a small command library outside this repository. It will be published as a package and is brought into phax under Apache-2.0. A command declares a name, a summary, its sources (`args`, `flags`, `stdin` holding one JSON document, `env`), each an Effect Schema with a policy for what it does not declare (`reject` or `strip`). It also declares an output contract with its policy, an exit code for each tagged error its run may fail with, a run, and an optional pure render. A program names its commands and two runner codes: `refused` (an unknown command, an undeclared argument or option, a source that does not decode) and `defect` (anything no command declared). A command may answer with `refused` and never with `defect`. A program where the two collide is refused before anything runs. The process is data (`Io`), so a conformance suite can prove a runner without spawning a process. The one runner built so far parses the command line with Commander, building a fresh tree inside each call.
problem: An agent, a script or the Claude Code mod cannot rely on phax for a machine answer. Most commands have no `--json`. Where `--json` exists, the document may be unversioned (`plans lint`, `plans overview`, `plans status`), may print on one line (`artifact decide`), or may be refused depending on another flag. `artifact status`, which the mod needs for every spec and plan, has no JSON at all. Errors are free text on stderr, so a caller can act on a failure only by parsing English. Exit 1 means four different things: an unknown option, the phase guard, a command's own failure, and an unexpected crash. Nothing publishes what a command reads, answers or fails with. The CLI contract (`phax.usage.kdl`) is whatever the Commander tree happens to hold, and the library phax is adopting gives the generator no tree to walk. The prerequisite of the `claude-code-mod` spec (`artifact-status`, a versioned `plan-overview`, each run's pull request) cannot be met command by command without repeating the drift that caused the problem.

productGoal.statement: Every phax command runs under a contract: what it reads, what it answers and how it fails. The runner enforces the contract identically on every command. `--json` always writes the command's versioned output document on stdout and its errors as JSON lines on stderr. `--json-schema` prints the contracts, and `phax.usage.kdl` is written from them. The three answers the Claude Code mod reads (`artifact status`, `plans overview`, the run list) come first, versioned and published. Nothing a person sees, nothing a migrated command declares, and no exit code phax documents changes on the way.
productGoal.guidingRule: A command's machine answer is its declared contract, never what the command chose to print.

terminology.definition: The operator's library that defines commands as contracts and runs them. phax ports it to Effect 3 as one internal module, with its conformance suite, until the published package replaces the port.

Everything a command declares: its name and summary, its sources with their schemas and policies, its output contract and policy, the exit code of each tagged error it may fail with, and its long help, examples and completion.
One input a command declares: `args` (positionals, typed by position), `flags`, `stdin` (one document) or `env`. Each source has a schema and a policy.
What a source or output does with what its schema does not declare: `reject` refuses the call, `strip` drops it.
The schema of the value a command answers. Under `--json` its encoded form is written to stdout, and it is published as the command's JSON Schema.
A command's optional pure view of its output for a person, given the output and the terminal and returning text.

The part of the library that parses the command line, decodes each declared source, runs the command, encodes and renders its output, and maps every failure to an exit code. It owns `--json` and `--json-schema`.
The program's exit code for a call the runner refuses before the command runs: an unknown command, an undeclared argument or option, or a source that does not decode. phax's value is 1.
The program's exit code for a failure no command declared, including an output that does not encode. No command may declare this code.
Under `--json`, one JSON object on one stderr line for one failure, carrying its `kind` and no `$schema`.
A flag a command binds to its `stdin` source, named for the document it carries. Its value is optional: absent means stdin is not read, alone or `-` means stdin, and a path means that file.
A file a command writes, reported in its output by its path from the repository root, its `$schema` and its `sha256:<hex>` digest, never by its content.

requirements.title: The library, ported
requirements.statement: The system shall carry the command library ported to Effect 3 as one internal module, which passes the library's conformance suite and differs from the library only where Effect 3 requires it or where a decided question of this spec changes it.

requirements.title: Every command under the runner
requirements.statement: The system shall register every command of `phax.usage.kdl` through the runner, so that no phax command definition refers to Commander.

requirements.title: A person's view
requirements.statement: WHEN a command is invoked without `--json` THE system SHALL write the command's render of its output to stdout, or the output's JSON when the command declares no render.

requirements.title: --json writes the output document
requirements.statement: WHEN a command is invoked with `--json` THE system SHALL write only the encoded form of the command's output to stdout, indented by two spaces and followed by one trailing newline.

requirements.title: Documents are versioned
requirements.statement: The system shall give every document a command writes under `--json` a `$schema` key first, naming the output contract's published JSON Schema.

requirements.title: --json and --json-schema are the runner's
requirements.statement: IF a command declares a flag named `--json` or `--json-schema`, or declares the `defect` code for one of its errors, THEN the system SHALL refuse the program before any command runs.

requirements.title: Errors as JSON lines
requirements.statement: WHILE a command runs under `--json` THE system SHALL write each error the command fails with to stderr as one JSON line carrying `kind`, the error's tag and its fields, and no `$schema`.

requirements.title: Refusals as JSON lines
requirements.statement: WHILE a call is made with `--json` THE system SHALL write each refusal to stderr as one JSON line carrying `kind`, the refused source, the path of the field that failed and what was expected.

requirements.title: Refused calls
requirements.statement: IF a call names an unknown command, carries an undeclared argument or option, or carries a source that does not decode, THEN the system SHALL exit with the `refused` code 1 without running the command, unless that command's help documents another code for that value.

requirements.title: Defects
requirements.statement: IF a command fails with an error it did not declare, or its output does not encode with its output contract, THEN the system SHALL exit with the `defect` code, which no command answers.

requirements.title: Documented codes stay
requirements.statement: The system shall exit with the code a command's help documents today for every outcome that help names.

requirements.title: phax --json-schema
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax --json-schema` runs THE system SHALL print every command's contract: its sources' JSON Schemas and policies, its output's JSON Schema, each error tag with its exit code, and the `refused` and `defect` codes.

requirements.title: <command> --json-schema
requirements.statement: WHEN a command is invoked with `--json-schema` THE system SHALL print that command's contract alone and run nothing else.

requirements.title: Line shapes published
requirements.statement: The system shall publish the shapes of the error line and the refusal line once, with the contracts, in the schemas package.

requirements.title: A document always read
requirements.statement: WHERE a command declares a `stdin` source with no bound flag THE system SHALL read the document from stdin on every call, and refuse the call at once when stdin is a terminal.

requirements.title: A document behind a flag
requirements.statement: WHERE a command binds a flag to its `stdin` source THE system SHALL read no stdin when the flag is absent, read stdin when the flag is given alone or with `-`, refusing at once on a terminal, and read the named file without opening stdin when the flag carries a path.

requirements.title: Written files are output
requirements.statement: WHEN a command writes files THE system SHALL list each in its output with its path from the repository root, its `$schema` and its `sha256:<hex>` digest.

requirements.title: Failing part way
requirements.statement: IF a command fails after writing some files THEN the system SHALL name each file already written in its error.

requirements.title: One document, --out
requirements.statement: WHERE a command writes a single document THE system SHALL take `--out <path|->`, writing the document to the path or, with `-`, to stdout.

requirements.title: artifact status --json
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact status <path> --json` runs THE system SHALL write an `artifact-status` document holding the artifact's kind, status, legal transitions, approval with its approver and whether it was edited since, authoring mode with sidecar sync, and its open and arbitrated questions.

requirements.title: plans overview --json versioned
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax plans overview <plan> --json` runs THE system SHALL write a `plan-overview` document whose content is today's overview with `$schema` first.

requirements.title: plans lint --json versioned
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax plans lint <plan> --json` runs THE system SHALL write a `plan-lint` document whose content is today's report with `$schema` first, exiting 1 when a finding is an error, as today.

requirements.title: Each run's pull request
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax ls --json` runs THE system SHALL give each run of the `run-list` document a `pullRequest` holding the number and URL of the pull request phax opened for it, or null when phax opened none.

requirements.title: Today's --json documents kept
requirements.statement: The system shall keep, under the runner's `--json`, the document each command prints with `--json` today: byte for byte when it is versioned, with only a `$schema` added first and the runner's layout when it is not.

requirements.title: phax.usage.kdl from the contracts
requirements.statement: The system shall write `phax.usage.kdl` from the program's contracts, declaring for every migrated command the same arguments, options, help, long help, examples and completion it declares today, and `--json` and `--json-schema` once as the program's flags.

requirements.title: --help kept
requirements.statement: WHEN a command is invoked with `--help` THE system SHALL print its summary, arguments, options, long help and examples.

surface.summary: Every phax command accepts `--json` and prints its versioned answer on stdout, with each error as one JSON line on stderr.
surface.before:
$ phax artifact approve docs/specs/2611031200-command-contracts.md --by operator --json
error: unknown option '--json'
Run `phax --help` for usage.
$? = 1

surface.summary: Running `phax --json-schema`, or `--json-schema` on one command, prints what each command reads, answers and fails with, as JSON Schemas and exit codes.
Running `phax artifact status --json` prints a spec's or plan's status, approval, authoring and questions as one versioned document.

surface.summary: `phax plans overview --json` now prints a versioned `plan-overview` document that starts with its `$schema`.
`phax plans lint --json` now prints a versioned `plan-lint` document that starts with its `$schema`, and still exits 1 when a finding is an error.
The run list from `phax ls --json` now gives each run the pull request phax opened for it.
The CLI spec in `phax.usage.kdl` is written from the command contracts and lists `--json` and `--json-schema` once, as flags of every command.
The schemas package now publishes `artifact-status`, `plan-overview`, `plan-lint`, `run-list` 0.33.0, each command's output document, and the shapes of the error and refusal lines.

import { formats } from "@lbdremy/phax-schemas";
formats["artifact-status"]; // 0.33.0
formats["plan-overview"];   // 0.33.0
formats["plan-lint"];       // 0.33.0
formats["run-list"];        // 0.33.0
formats["error-line"];      // 0.33.0

nonGoals: phax's move to Effect 4, and replacing the port with the published package: a later spec.
The Claude Code mod itself; this spec only provides what it reads.
A flag that only validates a command's input and stops before running it.
Renaming any command or flag, including turning `phax ls` into `phax runs list`.
Changing what any command does, or its text output for a person, beyond its output being drawn by its render.
Changing `phax artifact schema spec|plan|verdicts`: it keeps printing the document formats.
Choosing `--json` from whether stdout is a terminal: `--json` stays an explicit flag.
Keeping old unversioned `--json` documents readable as they were: they gain `$schema`, with no back-compat shim.

acceptanceCriteria.name: The port passes the conformance suite
acceptanceCriteria.given: the ported command library in phax
acceptanceCriteria.when: the library's conformance suite runs against the runner
acceptanceCriteria.then: every conformance case passes

acceptanceCriteria.name: No command imports Commander
acceptanceCriteria.given: phax's source after migration
acceptanceCriteria.then: no command definition imports Commander, and every command of `phax.usage.kdl` is registered through the runner

acceptanceCriteria.name: Text output unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that printed text before migration, such as `phax plans overview <plan>`
acceptanceCriteria.when: it runs without `--json` on the same input
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is byte for byte the text it printed before migration

acceptanceCriteria.name: No render prints JSON
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that declares an output contract and no render
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is the output's JSON

acceptanceCriteria.name: --json layout
acceptanceCriteria.given: any command that succeeds
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout holds exactly one JSON document, indented by two spaces, ending in one newline, with `$schema` as its first key and decoding against the published schema it names

acceptanceCriteria.name: Reserved flags and code refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a program in which one command declares a `--json` flag, a `--json-schema` flag, or the `defect` code for an error
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused before any command runs, naming the command

acceptanceCriteria.name: An error is one JSON line
acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact with open questions
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 12, stdout is empty, and stderr holds one JSON line whose `kind` is `error`, carrying the error's tag and fields and no `$schema`

acceptanceCriteria.name: A refusal is one JSON line
acceptanceCriteria.given: a call with an undeclared option
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 1 without running lint, and stderr holds one JSON line whose `kind` is `refused`, naming the source `flags`, the path of the option and what was expected

acceptanceCriteria.name: Unknown command refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: no command named `frobnicate`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 1

acceptanceCriteria.name: A documented value code wins
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phax artifact approve` documents exit 12 for a malformed `--by`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 12, not 1

acceptanceCriteria.name: An undeclared failure is a defect
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command whose run fails with an error it did not declare, or whose output does not encode
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits with the `defect` code, which differs from 1 and from every code a command declares

acceptanceCriteria.name: Documented codes kept
acceptanceCriteria.given: the exit codes each command's help documents before migration
acceptanceCriteria.when: each documented outcome is reproduced after migration
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits with the code its help documents

acceptanceCriteria.name: Every contract printed
acceptanceCriteria.given: the migrated program
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints one contract per command of `phax.usage.kdl`, each with its sources' schemas and policies, its output schema and its error tags with their codes, plus the `refused` and `defect` codes, and exits 0

acceptanceCriteria.name: One contract printed
acceptanceCriteria.given: any command
acceptanceCriteria.when: it runs with `--json-schema`, as in `phax plans lint --json-schema`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints that command's contract alone, runs nothing, writes nothing and exits 0

acceptanceCriteria.name: Line shapes in the package
acceptanceCriteria.given: the schemas package built for the release
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exports the JSON Schemas of the error line and the refusal line, and every line from `ac-error-line` and `ac-refusal-line` decodes against its shape

acceptanceCriteria.name: A terminal is never waited on
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that reads a `stdin` document with no bound flag, run with a terminal on stdin
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused at once with exit 1 and never waits on input

acceptanceCriteria.name: Bound flag reading
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phax artifact decide <path> --verdicts <file|-> --by operator`
acceptanceCriteria.when: it runs with a path, with `-` and a piped file, with `-` and a terminal, and without `--verdicts`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the path's file is read and stdin is never opened; the pipe is read; the terminal is refused at once; and without the flag stdin is not read

acceptanceCriteria.name: Written files listed
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that writes files, such as `phax artifact approve <path> --by operator`
acceptanceCriteria.then: its output lists each file written with its repo-root path, its `$schema` and a `sha256:<hex>` digest equal to the file's digest, and not its content

acceptanceCriteria.name: Part-way failure names what was written
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that fails after writing a file, such as an approval whose commit fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: its error line names each file already written

acceptanceCriteria.name: --out writes the single document
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command that writes a single document
acceptanceCriteria.then: the document is written to the path, then to stdout

acceptanceCriteria.name: artifact status document
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved headless spec with one arbitrated question
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is an `artifact-status` document whose `$schema` is `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/artifact-status/0.33.0.json`, holding kind `spec`, status `Approved`, its legal transitions, its approval with approver and `editedSince`, authoring `headless` with its sidecar sync, and its questions, matching what the text output reports

acceptanceCriteria.name: plan-overview versioned
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan that `phax plans overview` lays out
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is today's overview with `$schema` `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/plan-overview/0.33.0.json` as its first key and no other change

acceptanceCriteria.name: plan-lint versioned, exit kept
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan with one error finding
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is today's report with `$schema` `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/plan-lint/0.33.0.json` first, and it exits 1

acceptanceCriteria.name: Run list carries the pull request
acceptanceCriteria.given: one run phax published a pull request for and one it did not
acceptanceCriteria.then: the `run-list` document is stamped `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/run-list/0.33.0.json`, the first run's `pullRequest` holds that pull request's number and URL, and the second's is null

acceptanceCriteria.name: Versioned documents byte for byte
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command printing a versioned document with `--json` before migration
acceptanceCriteria.when: it runs with `--json` on the same state after migration
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is byte for byte what it printed before, except where this spec adds a field

acceptanceCriteria.name: Usage spec parity
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phax.usage.kdl` before migration
acceptanceCriteria.when: the usage generator writes it from the contracts
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file is the generator's output, and every command declares the same arguments, options, help, long help, examples and completion as before, with `--json` and `--json-schema` declared once as program flags instead of per command

acceptanceCriteria.name: --help kept
acceptanceCriteria.given: a command with long help and examples, such as `phax plans overview`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints the summary, the argument, the options, the long help and the examples

openQuestions.question: Which code is phax's `defect`? Today an unknown option, the phase guard and an unexpected crash all exit 1, and the library forbids `refused` and `defect` from sharing a code.

options.label: `refused` stays 1; `defect` becomes 70 (sysexits EX_SOFTWARE), a code no command uses
options.abandons: exit 1 as the code of an unexpected crash: a script that took 1 to mean "phax broke" now sees 70, and phax's code table grows by one

options.label: `defect` keeps 1; `refused` moves to 64 (EX_USAGE)
options.abandons: the 1 phax documents for the phase guard and Commander's 1 for an unknown option, which scripts and docs already rely on, and every command that answers 1 would collide with `defect`

openQuestions.rationale: Moving the crash code changes only an outcome phax never documented. Moving `refused` breaks documented codes, which the operator settled must stay, and leaves `defect` sharing 1 with commands like `plans lint`.

openQuestions.question: How does a command answer a document together with a non-zero exit, as `plans lint` does today (the report, then exit 1 when a finding is an error)? The library maps failures to codes and successes to 0.

options.label: The output contract lets a command answer its value and the exit code it ends with (lint: its report, and 1 when it holds an error)
options.abandons: fidelity to the library as written: a change Effect 3 did not ask for, which must be carried upstream before the package can replace the port

options.label: Error findings become a tagged error exiting 1, the report carried in the error line on stderr and stdout left empty
options.abandons: `phax plans lint --json > lint.json` holding the report when it matters most: the `plan-lint` document would exist only for a plan with no error

openQuestions.rationale: A lint report that disappears from stdout exactly when it has errors defeats the machine answer this spec exists for. The library change is small and belongs upstream anyway.

openQuestions.question: `artifact new spec|plan --brief <file|->` reads a Markdown brief, but the library's `stdin` source is one JSON document. How does the brief come in?

options.label: The `stdin` source can declare a text document: `--brief` is its bound flag and follows the bound-flag rules (terminal refused, path reads the file)
options.abandons: the library's rule that stdin is one JSON document: a second document kind in the port, to carry upstream

options.label: `--brief` stays a plain option holding a path or `-`, and the command reads the file or stdin itself through phax's ports
options.abandons: one way of reading stdin: `--brief -` escapes the runner's terminal refusal, and `--json-schema` does not show the brief as the command's document

openQuestions.rationale: The brief is the command's content, which is what the stdin source models. Reading it outside the runner brings back the per-command input handling the contracts remove.

openQuestions.question: Under `--json`, errors and refusals are JSON lines on stderr. What about the other stderr lines commands write today: warnings (`Warning: architecture provider failed: …`), progress (`phax run`, `decide --verdicts`) and record lines?

options.label: Under `--json` every stderr line is a JSON line: warnings and progress get their own `kind` beside `error` and `refused`, with published shapes
options.abandons: readable progress for a person watching a `--json` run, plus fidelity to the library, which gains warning and progress lines

options.label: Only errors and refusals are JSON lines; warnings and progress stay text, and a reader keeps the lines that parse as an object with a `kind`
options.abandons: a stderr an agent can read line by line without guessing: any text line starting with `{` is ambiguous, and a warning cannot be acted on by its fields

openQuestions.rationale: The JSON lines exist for an agent that runs the command and acts on what it sees. A stream mixing prose and JSON makes it guess. A person wanting readable progress runs without `--json`.

settled: The library is ported to Effect 3 into one internal module of phax, with its conformance suite. The plan names the module's place.
Every command moves in this spec. The plan orders them by family, `artifact status`, `plans overview`, `plans lint` and `ls` first.

`--json` and `--json-schema` are the runner's. The per-command `--json` options of `ls`, `plans status|overlap|lint|overview|estimate`, `artifact decide` and the others become the program's flag. As a consequence, `artifact decide`'s refusal of `--json` without `--verdicts` ends: interactive decide under `--json` writes its output document like every other command.
The run list stays `phax ls`, and its document stays `run-list`, gaining `pullRequest` at 0.33.0.
`refused` is 1, the code of Commander's refusal and of the phase guard today.

`phax --usage` keeps working, and `phax.usage.kdl` is the generator's output from the program's contracts. Command groups, long help, examples and completion move into the command definitions, and the library gains what it lacks for them.
Output contracts are where the published JSON Schemas of these documents come from, versioned and snapshotted like every other format in the schemas package.
open: Each interactive command's output contract (`enter`, `shell`, `open`, `review-code`, interactive `decide`, `init`): what it answers after handing the terminal to a session, within the rules above.
Which commands write a single document and so take `--out`. None may lose an argument or option it declares today.
The exact field names of `artifact-status`, of the contract `--json-schema` prints, and of the error and refusal lines, within the shapes shown in §6.
constraints: Port the library changed only where Effect 3 requires it or where a decided §9 question changes it, so the published package can replace the port.
A command whose help documents an exit code for a malformed value (`--by`, `--security`, a slug) keeps that code: it decodes the value's raw form and checks it in its run.
A document that is versioned today stays byte for byte under `--json`, except for the fields this spec adds.
Each command's text output for a person stays byte for byte, now drawn by its render.
No back-compat shim: unversioned documents gain `$schema` and are not also emitted in their old shape.
The architecture audit enforces that no command definition imports Commander.

docsPage.reader: An agent author or a script writer who runs phax commands and acts on their answers and failures.
